analysis.investment_thesis: AJC Jewel fails both Magic Formula tests: earnings yield of ~5.5% (1/18 P/E) is below the 6% minimum, and ROE of 0.22% implies ROIC near zero — neither cheap nor a good business. This is the opposite of what the formula seeks.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 56.33% indicates skin in the game.
Operates in structurally growing Indian jewelry sector.
Small base may allow optical growth if execution improves.
key_risks: ROE of 0.22% — capital is earning essentially nothing, fatal for Magic Formula.
Earnings yield ~5.5% (P/E 18) is below my 6% attractiveness floor.
Jewelry manufacturing is capital-intensive with thin margins and weak pricing power.
red_flags: ROE of 0.22% suggests either negligible EBIT or bloated capital base.
P/E 18 with sub-1% ROE implies the market is pricing optionality, not earnings.
Young company (2018) with no long ROIC track record to validate economics.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks stocks by earnings yield (EBIT/EV) and return on capital. AJC Jewel's P/E of 18 caps earnings yield at ~5.5% — below my 6% floor and nowhere near the 12%+ I want. More damning, a 0.22% ROE means capital is effectively idle; ROIC is almost certainly in low single digits, not the 20%+ threshold that defines a 'good business.' The formula is designed to find companies that are both cheap AND good. This is neither.

Jewelry manufacturing is inherently capital-intensive (gold inventory, working capital cycles), making high ROIC difficult without strong brand pricing power — which a 2018-vintage micro-cap does not have. With a tiny INR 52 Cr market cap, thin liquidity, and no evidence of compounding economics, a systematic quant screen would filter this out immediately. Pass.
